System: Fresh human PBMC; healthy volunteer Phase I
Condition: hPBMC dose-response; clinical SC dosing 100–200 mg highlighted
Result: High human inflammatory response; clinical development discontinued; hPBMC identifies risk missed by rodent/NHP
Mechanism/Receptor: B-cell dependent; chloroquine-sensitive; likely human TLR9 despite no canonical CpG
Scientific Interpretation: High-value positive benchmark for human-specific ASO immunotoxicity.
Caution/Limit: Donor-dependent bell-shaped response; fresh PBMC needed; benchmark-relative rather than universal absolute cutoff.

Result: Low-inflammatory benchmark relative to ISIS 353512
Evidence Level: Primary human in vitro + prior clinical experience
Scientific Interpretation: Useful negative/low-risk reference benchmark, not an absolute inert control.
Caution/Limit: Do not equate 'low risk' with zero pathway activity.

Condition: 5-10-5 MOE gapmer; clinical doses up to 400 mg/week, later 600 mg reported
Result: Minimal immune stimulation and better clinical tolerability than 353512
Mechanism/Receptor: Sequence and shorter unmodified gap context
Scientific Interpretation: Strong clinically anchored low-risk ASO comparator.
Caution/Limit: Exact sequence resides in Supplementary Table S1, not available in current PDF.

Condition: Same context as 353512 with unmodified gap reduced from 14 to 10 bases
Result: Response became similar to low-risk ISIS 104838
Mechanism/Receptor: Unmodified PS DNA gap length contributes to risk
Scientific Interpretation: Gap length is a predictor, but sequence still independently matters.
Caution/Limit: Do not rewrite as 'CpG + gap ≥14' because 353512 lacks a canonical CpG motif.

System: Human PBMC vs hirudin whole blood
Result: PBMC and whole blood can produce materially different cytokine profiles; WBA better mirrored reported human in-vivo IFN-α for these CpGs
Evidence Level: Primary human in vitro with clinical comparison
Scientific Interpretation: Cell system is a model feature/metadata variable, not a nuisance to collapse away.
Caution/Limit: Do not merge PBMC and whole-blood measurements without assay context.

Result: Three 2'-O-methyl modifications markedly reduced cytokine induction in both systems
Scientific Interpretation: Position-specific modification can suppress immunostimulation.
Caution/Limit: Exact methylated positions must be preserved; 'percent 2'OMe' alone is insufficient.

Result: Minimal effective concentration varied substantially with delivery agent
Scientific Interpretation: Carrier/delivery is a predictor/confounder and should be part of the schema.
Caution/Limit: Sequence-only prediction will misattribute delivery effects.

Result: GU-rich sequences show TLR7/8 profile; AU-rich sequences can preferentially drive TLR8-type proinflammatory responses
Scientific Interpretation: TLR7 and TLR8 should be separate outcomes or multi-label targets.
Caution/Limit: A single cytokine OR-label erases receptor-specific biology.

Result: TLR8-specific RNA responses were human/bovine but not mouse/rat/porcine
Scientific Interpretation: Species is mandatory metadata and animal negatives cannot be treated as human negatives.
Caution/Limit: Directly relevant to challenge emphasis on human-based systems.

Result: 2'OMe-A was strongly suppressive; 2'F-A also suppressive; 2'OMe-G effective with few residues; 2'OMe-U required more context; C modifications were ineffective
Scientific Interpretation: Modification identity, modified base, strand and count/position should be explicit features.
Caution/Limit: Reject universal '25–30% 2'OMe is sufficient' rule.

Result: 2'F modifications were generally more tolerated for knockdown than 2'OMe, but immune effects varied by nucleotide
Scientific Interpretation: Safety and efficacy labels should remain separate outcomes.
Caution/Limit: A 'protective modification' can reduce potency depending on strand/position.

Result: RNA40 induced IFN-α plus proinflammatory cytokines; RNA42 induced proinflammatory cytokines but failed to induce IFN-α
Mechanism/Receptor: TLR7/8; GU composition and cell-type specificity
Scientific Interpretation: Cytokine-specific labels are biologically non-equivalent.
Caution/Limit: Do not infer one pathway from an overall POS label.

Result: IFN-α/TLR7 response lost while IL-6/TLR8 response remained
Scientific Interpretation: Single modification can switch receptor specificity rather than make an oligo globally 'safe'.
Caution/Limit: Directly contradicts 'GU-rich + 2'OMe means safe'.

Result: Did not reproduce the TLR7-suppressive effect of 2'-O-methyl-G
Scientific Interpretation: 2'F cannot be treated as globally equivalent to 2'OMe.
Caution/Limit: Position/base/context are essential.

Result: Inhibited TLR7/8/9 signaling/cytokines
Scientific Interpretation: Dataset needs an immunomodulatory-direction class: agonist, antagonist, potentiator, inert.
Caution/Limit: Antagonists are not ordinary NEG/safe examples.

Result: Full-length purity ~94–99% depending method; identity by MALDI-TOF; HPLC/CGE; endotoxin <0.075 EU/mg
Scientific Interpretation: Purity and endotoxin belong in the Phase 2 dataset because contamination can confound immunotoxicity.
Caution/Limit: Report method-specific purity, not a single undocumented purity flag.

Condition: Long in-vitro-transcribed RNAs; various nucleoside modifications
Result: Multiple modified nucleosides suppressed RNA sensing through TLR3/7/8 in a modification- and cell-type-dependent way
Scientific Interpretation: Supports chemistry-resolved modeling beyond motifs.
Caution/Limit: Long RNA findings should not be used as direct 15–30mer therapeutic labels without modality qualification.

Result: Unmethylated CpG motifs drove strong B-cell activation; methylation/inversion reduced activity in this system
Scientific Interpretation: Useful mechanistic anchor for CpG features.
Caution/Limit: Not a human therapeutic toxicity label; species and historical assay context must be explicit.

Result: Sequence/structure can create receptor antagonists even when oligos share features with agonists
Evidence Level: Review; primary sources should be retrieved for training rows
Scientific Interpretation: Useful taxonomy and sequence shortlist for antagonist class.
Caution/Limit: Do not train quantitative labels from review alone.

Condition: DOTAP; 4-point dose response; 21-nt strands with 3' overhangs
Result: U count in U-rich strand correlated with activity; stronger duplex hybridization correlated negatively; specific positions including G2/G13 mattered; TT overhangs enriched among low activity
Mechanism/Receptor: Endosomal TLR7/8 via denatured U-rich strand
Scientific Interpretation: Add strand-specific U content, duplex ΔG, positional nucleotides and overhang chemistry to features.
Caution/Limit: Full 207-sequence supplementary XLS is not embedded in the PDF and should be retrieved before claiming complete row-level coverage.

Result: CpG-only methylation increased TLR9 stimulation in the LNA version but abolished it in the non-LNA version; full C methylation reduced activity
Scientific Interpretation: CpG methylation is not a universal protection rule.
Caution/Limit: Interaction feature needed; avoid main-effect-only conclusion.

Result: Non-CpG SECA141 activated hTLR9 in sensitive THP1-hTLR9 cells; CpG-containing SECA166 was inactive
Scientific Interpretation: CpG presence is neither necessary nor sufficient for TLR9 activation in LNA gapmers.
Caution/Limit: Assay sensitivity matters; HEK-hTLR9 and THP1-hTLR9 gave different detection.

Condition: Partially overlapping non-CpG LNA gapmers sharing 15/19 residues
Result: SECA138 activated hTLR9 while SECA083 did not
Scientific Interpretation: Near-neighbor sequences can differ materially; sequence-family split is essential for model validation.
Caution/Limit: Random train/test split may leak near-neighbor information.

Result: LNA modifications could increase or decrease TLR9 activity depending on sequence and assay
Scientific Interpretation: Replace 'LNA increases TLR9 risk' with a sequence-dependent interaction statement.
Caution/Limit: Need exact modification positions, not just is_LNA boolean.

Result: 2'OMe-A/G/U (not C) could antagonize TLR7-mediated cytokine induction in trans; not simply inert
Scientific Interpretation: A modified oligo can suppress another oligo's signal; label as antagonist, not NEG.
Caution/Limit: Co-formulation/context can change observed phenotype.

Result: Little/no inhibition of Type B/C TLR9 response; Type A response inhibited
Scientific Interpretation: Pathway interactions are class-specific.
Caution/Limit: Avoid generalizing 2'OMe as a pan-TLR inhibitor.

Result: Single strands were generally more immunostimulatory than corresponding duplexes
Scientific Interpretation: Strand state (ss vs duplex) is a mandatory feature.
Caution/Limit: Duplex denaturation and carrier/endosomal exposure affect phenotype.

Result: Replacing uridine 2'-OH with 2'F, 2'deoxy or 2'OMe abrogated immune activation in the tested sequences
Scientific Interpretation: Supports uridine chemistry as a feature.
Caution/Limit: Do not universalize beyond tested sequences; Fucini/Jung show context dependence for other nucleotides/positions.

Result: ~50% of tested siRNAs induced cytokines; six were strong; siRNA27 strongest; siRNA32 low/non-stimulatory
Mechanism/Receptor: Sequence-dependent, chloroquine-sensitive endosomal signaling; TLR8 favored in monocytes
Scientific Interpretation: High-value positive/negative sequence panel.
Caution/Limit: Per-sequence labels beyond explicit controls need figure digitization or threshold protocol.

Result: Strong dose-dependent immunostimulation
Scientific Interpretation: Robust positive control candidate for siRNA/TLR8 module.
Caution/Limit: Delivery agent required; naked sequence was not stimulatory.

Result: Free siRNA produced little/no cytokine while DOTAP-complexed siRNA was strongly active
Scientific Interpretation: Sequence cannot be labeled toxic independently of delivery condition.
Caution/Limit: Core ML label should be experiment-level, not oligo-only.

Result: 95% of tested ASOs inhibited at least one of TLR7, TLR9 or cGAS by ≥30%; receptor-specific effects were sequence-dependent
Scientific Interpretation: The outcome space must include suppression/potentiation, not only stimulation.
Caution/Limit: Supplementary Tables S1/S2 are needed for complete 80-ASO sequence-level extraction.

Result: A-, B-, and C-class CpG ODNs produced distinct cytokine/cell profiles despite all signaling through TLR9
Scientific Interpretation: Do not collapse all TLR9 agonists into one homogeneous POS class.
Caution/Limit: ODN class, backbone pattern, palindrome/G-rich structure should be features.
